Rashi on Zevachim 8a:1:1.english: “And the priest shall take” - This is an expression of collection.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:11:1.hebrew: ואפי' לעופות - שחטו לשם חטאת עוף:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:11:1.english: And even for birds - If one slaughtered it for the sake of a bird sin-offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:13:1.hebrew: אף כל שהוא שלא לשמו - יצא שחטו לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:13:1.english: So too, any case where it is not for its own sake - This excludes [a case where it was slaughtered] for its own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:14:1.hebrew: חטאת ואשם לא - שחטו לשם חטאת ואשם, יהא פסול אפילו לשלמים:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:14:1.english: A sin offering and a guilt offering, no - If one slaughtered it for the sake of a sin offering or a guilt offering, it would be disqualified, even as a peace offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:15:1.hebrew: אלא לזבח רבויא הוא - אינו לשון כלל, ולא דרשי' ליה בכלל ופרט, שאין כללות ופרטות באין מרבוי לשון אלא ממשמעות המקראות. וכגון (ב"ק דף סג.) בכל אשר תאוה נפשך — כלל, וכן מן הבהמה — כלל, בקר וצאן — פרט. אבל לזבח שלמים — שתי תיבות דבוקות הן, כאילו כתיב לזבח השלמים, וקרא יתירא בעלמא הוא, דהוה מצי למכתב לשלמים. וכל מקרא של לשון ייתור אינו לכלל ופרט אלא לרבות, וכמאן דכתיב לשלמים וזבח דמי, דאיתרבו ליה כל הזבחים:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:15:1.english: Rather, "for a sacrifice" is an amplification - It is not a language of generalization, and we do not expound it by [the method of] generalization and detail, for generalizations and details do not come from an expression of amplification but from the meaning of the verses. For example, (Bava Kamma 63a) "in all that your soul desires" is a generalization, and likewise "from the animal" is a generalization, "cattle and flock" is a detail. But "for a peace-offering sacrifice" — these are two words joined together, as if it were written "for the sacrifice of the peace-offering," and the verse is merely superfluous, as it could have written "for peace-offerings." And any verse of superfluous language is not [expounded] as a generalization and detail but as an amplification; and it is as if it were written "for peace-offerings" and "sacrifice," such that all sacrifices are included in it.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:1:1.hebrew: חטאת דעבודת כוכבים - דכתיב בפ' שלח לך, ולא כתיב בהאי עניינא "לחטאת". וכן חטאת דשמיעת הקול, לא כתיב בההוא עניינא, דההוא עניינא בחטאת דשגגת כרת קיימא, כדילפינן בהוריות (דף ב.):
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:1:1.english: The sin offering of idol worship - As it is written in the portion of Shelach Lekha, and in that matter [the term "for a sin offering"] is not written. And likewise the sin offering of the hearing of the voice: [the term] is not written in that passage, since that passage deals with the sin offering for an unintentional transgression punishable by karet, as we derive in Horayot (2a).

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:1:2.hebrew: שמיעת הקול - שבועת העדות: "ושמעה קול אלה" (שמיעת הקול). ושבועת ביטוי, וטומאת מקדש וקדשיו — בחד עניינא כתיבי בקרבן עולה ויורד: "ושמעה קול אלה", "או נפש כי תשבע לבטא", "או נפש אשר תגע" וגו'. ומוקמא לה במסכת שבועות בטומאת מקדש וקדשיו:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:1:2.english: The hearing of the voice - [This refers to] the oath of testimony: "and he heard the voice of adjuration" (Leviticus 5:1). And the oath of utterance, and the defilement of the Temple and its sacred items — they are written in one matter, concerning the sliding-scale offering (the "offering of ascending and descending value"): "and he heard the voice of adjuration," "or a soul that swears, speaking [rashly]" (Leviticus 5:4), "or a soul that touches" (Leviticus 5:2), etc. And in tractate Shevuot, [the Gemara] establishes it as referring to defilement of the Temple and its sacred items.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:2:1.hebrew: אתיין במה הצד - מחטאת חלב וחטאת נזיר ומצורע, דכי פרכת: מה לחטאת חלב שכן כרת, חטאת נזיר ומצורע יוכיחו; מה לחטאת נזיר ומצורע שכן יש עמהן דמים אחרים, חטאת חלב תוכיח. הצד השוה שבהן כו' אף אני אביא חטאת דשמיעת הקול ומחטאת חלב. וחדא מהני לא אתיא, דאי מחטאת חלב וחטאת נזיר איכא למיפרך: מה להצד השוה שבהן שכן אינן באין בדלות, תאמר בשבועת ביטוי שהיא בעולה ויורד. אי מחטאת חלב וחטאת מצורע איכא למיפרך: מה להצד השוה שבהן שכן אינן בשאלה, תאמר בשבועה שישנה בשאלה:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:2:1.english: They are derived through "what is the common element" - From the sin offering for forbidden fat, and the sin offering of a nazirite and of a leper. For when you refute: What about the sin offering for forbidden fat? It is because it carries karet. The sin offerings of the nazirite and the leper will prove [otherwise]. What about the sin offerings of the nazirite and the leper? It is because they have other [accompanying] offerings. The sin offering for forbidden fat will prove [otherwise]. "The common element among them," etc. — so too I will bring the sin offering for [violating the oath of] hearing a voice [of adjuration], from the sin offering for forbidden fat. And one of these alone would not suffice to derive it: for if it were derived from the sin offering for forbidden fat and the sin offering of the nazirite, one could refute: What about the common element among them? It is because they are not brought on a sliding scale (according to means); would you say the same of an oath of utterance, which is [brought] as a sliding-scale offering — an animal, bird, or flour offering, according to means? If from the sin offering for forbidden fat and the sin offering of the leper, one could refute: What about the common element among them? It is because they do not [apply] to a case of forgetfulness (an inadvertent act); would you say the same of an oath, which does apply to a case of forgetfulness?

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:1.hebrew: שלא לשמו פסול - כדאמרי' (לעיל זבחים דף ז:):
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:1.english: Not for its sake, it is unfit - As we said (above, Zevachim 7b).

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:2.hebrew: בשאר ימות השנה לשמו פסול - כדאמרי' במס' פסחים (דף סא.): אם שחטו קודם חצות, פסול, דכתיב "בין הערבים", וכמה פעמים שנה הכתוב בקביעות זמנו בי"ד "בין הערבים":
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:2.english: During the rest of the days of the year, [sacrificing it] for its own sake is unfit - As we say in tractate Pesachim (61a): If one slaughtered it before midday, it is unfit, as it is written, "between the evenings," and the verse repeated several times the fixing of its time on the fourteenth, "between the evenings."

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:3.english: Not for its sake, it is fit - As [the Gemara] explains as it proceeds.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:5:1.hebrew: מנהני מילי - דבשאר ימות השנה שלא לשמו כשר:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:5:1.english: From where [are] these matters - that during the rest of the days of the year, [a Paschal offering sacrificed] not for its own sake is valid.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:5:2.hebrew: ואם מן הצאן קרבנו כו' - לאו קרא יתירא קא דריש, אלא משמעותא דקרא משמע ליה הכי: ואם דבר הבא מן הצאן — דהיינו פסח, שאינו בא אלא מן הצאן — היה קרבנו, הרי הוא לזבח שלמים. ועל כרחך שלא בזמנו קאמר, דאי בזמנו הא ילפינן ליה לעיל דפסול:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:5:2.english: "And if his offering is of the flock," etc. - He is not expounding a superfluous verse; rather, the implication of the verse conveys this to him: And if something that comes from the flock — that is, the Paschal offering, which comes only from the flock — was his offering, it is [valid] as a sacrifice of peace offerings. And you must say that it is speaking of [a Paschal offering sacrificed] not at its [proper] time, for if it were at its [proper] time, we already derive above that it is disqualified.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:6:1.hebrew: ואימא שלמים אין כו' - שחטו לשם שלמים, ליתכשר; אבל שחטו לשם עולה, ליפסיל! וברייתא קתני שלא לשמו כשר, ואפילו שחטו לשם עולה או לשם חטאת:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:6:1.english: And say: peace offerings, yes, etc. - If one slaughtered it for the sake of a peace offering, let it be valid; but if one slaughtered it for the sake of a burnt offering, let it be disqualified! Yet the baraita teaches that [if slaughtered] not for its own sake, it is valid — even if one slaughtered it for the sake of a burnt offering or a sin offering:

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:6:2.hebrew: לזבח - קרא יתירא הוא, דמצי למכתב "לשלמים":
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:6:2.english: For a sacrifice - It is a redundant verse, for it could have written "for a peace offering."

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:7:1.hebrew: אימא לכל דשחיט להוי כוותיה - שחטו לשם עולה, יהא עולה, דהא אתרבי ליה "כל זבח":
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:7:1.english: Say: for whatever [purpose] one slaughters, it should be like it - If one slaughtered it for the sake of a burnt offering, it should be a burnt offering, for "any sacrifice" has been included with regard to it.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:8:1.hebrew: ה"ג אי הוה כתיב לשלמים וזבח כדקא אמרת - דאי כתב הכי, הוה משמע יהא כשלמים או כשאר זבח:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:8:1.english: This is the correct reading: If it had been written “for peace offerings and a sacrifice,” as you say - For if it had been written this way, it would imply: Let it be like a peace offering, or like any other sacrifice.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:8:2.hebrew: השתא דכתיב לזבח שלמים - הכי משמע: לכל זבח שיזבחנו לשמו, שלמים יהיה:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:8:2.english: Now that it is written “for a sacrifice of peace offerings” - This is what it means: for any sacrifice that one slaughters for its name [i.e., for the sake of peace offerings], it will be a peace offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:9:1.hebrew: ואימא לזבח כלל כו' - אמאי דריש להאי זבח שלמים הכי? דרוש הכי: דבר הבא מן הצאן יהא לכל הזבחים כלל, שכשר שלא לשמו. כי הדר כתב שלמים, פרט, שלא הכשרתיו בעקירת שמו אלא א"כ שחטו לשלמים, אבל שחטו לשם זבח אחר — פסול:
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:9:1.english: And say: “for a sacrifice” is a generalization, etc. - Why does he expound this “sacrifice… of peace offerings” in this way? Expound it thus: An item that comes from the flock is a generalization for all sacrifices, [meaning] that it is valid even if not offered for its own sake. When [the verse] then writes “peace offerings,” a detail, [it teaches] that you have not made it valid through uprooting its [proper] name unless he slaughtered it for the sake of a peace offering; but if he slaughtered it for the sake of another sacrifice, it is invalid.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:15:1.hebrew: אלא לזבח רבויא הוא - משמע ליה לגמרא שהוא רבויא, כדאמר (ב"ק דף סג.): בכל כללא, כל רבויא. דמשמע ליה לחלק בין "כל" ל"בכל". הילכך לא דרשינן ליה בכללא ופרטא, אלא בריבה ומיעט. ובקונטרס האריך בפירושו:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:15:1.english: Rather, "for a sacrifice" is an amplification - The Gemara understands that it is an amplification, as it says (Bava Kamma 63a): "[The word] 'be-khol' is a generalization; [the word] 'kol' is an amplification," for it understands to distinguish between "kol" and "be-khol." Therefore, we do not expound it by [the method of] generalization and detail, but by [the method of] amplification and restriction. And in the Kuntres [Rashi's commentary], [Rashi] elaborated in his explanation:

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:1:1.hebrew: חטאת דעבודת כוכבים אתיא מחטאת חלב שכן כרת כמותה - יש ספרים שכתוב בהן: "חטאת דעבודת כוכבים וטומאת מקדש וקדשיו", ואינו נראה; דאע"ג דכרת כמותה, מכל מקום איכא למיפרך: מה לחטאת חלב שכן אינה באה בדלות, כדפרכינן לעיל גבי חטאת מצורע:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:1:1.english: The sin offering for idol worship is derived from the sin offering for forbidden fat, since [the transgression] carries karet like it - There are books in which it is written: "The sin offering for idol worship, and for the defilement of the Temple and its sacred foods." But this does not seem [correct], for even though [that transgression] carries karet like it, nevertheless one can refute [the derivation]: What is [true] of the sin offering for forbidden fat is that it is not brought on a sliding scale [according to the person's means], as we refuted above with regard to the sin offering of a leper.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:1:2.hebrew: שמיעת קול - דלא כתיב "לחטאתו" גבי עבודה, מנלן עכובא? אבל כתיב "לחטאת" על דברים אחרים, ואין בכך כלום:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:1:2.english: Hearing of the voice - [Regarding the sin offerings for hearing the voice and the others,] where "for his sin offering" is not written with regard to the service, from where do we derive that it is indispensable? But "for a sin offering" is written with regard to other matters, and this amounts to nothing.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:2:1.hebrew: (ה"ג) הנך כולהו אתיין במה הצד - הקשה רבינו תם: מה להנך שכן אין באין בדלי דלות, תאמר בהנך? ותירץ: כיון דדלי דלות גופיה פסולה שלא לשמה — היינו מנחת חוטא דפסולה שלא לשמה, כדתנן בריש מנחות (דף ב.), ומפיק לן מדכתיב "כי חטאת היא" — אין סברא שמה שבאין בדלי דלות יגרום להם בעשירות להיות כשירין שלא לשמן, כיון שהדלי דלות עצמן פסול. וקשה: א"כ לעיל דפריך גבי מצורע "מה להנך שכן אינן באין בדלות, תאמר במצורע" — מאי קושיא? והלא דלות היינו חטאת העוף, וחטאת העוף פסולה שלא לשמה, כדתנן בפרק קדשי קדשים (לקמן זבחים דף סד:), ומפיק ליה בתורת כהנים מ"חטאת היא"; וכיון דפסולה בדלות, היאך יש לה לגרום בעשירות הכשר שלא לשמה? ואם תאמר: והא בחטאת חלב למדה משלמים בהיקש למצוה, והיכי ילפי' שאר חטאות במה הצד? הא בעיא היא לקמן פרק איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נ.): אי דבר הלמד בהיקש חוזר ומלמד בבנין אב? לאו פירכא היא כלל, דכולהו חטאות נמי ילפי' למצוה משלמים, ולעכב הוא דילפינן בשאר חטאות מהנך, דכתיב עכובא בגופייהו. ואם תאמר: וחטאות הצבור, כגון שעירי ראשי חדשים ומועדות, מנלן? הא לא אתו במה הצד, דמה להנך שכן שנוי בעלים פוסל בהן, מה שאין כן בקרבן צבור, כדאמר לעיל (זבחים דף ד.) דשנוי בעלים ליתא בצבור כביחיד. אע"ג דלא שייך שנוי בעלים בצבור, מ"מ פירכא טובה היא, כדאשכחן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף ה:): "מה לכסף שכן פודין בו הקדשות ומעשר שני, תאמר בחופה"; וכן פרק החובל (ב"ק דף פח.): "מה לאשה שאינה במילה". ועוד קשה: חטאות פנימיות, לרבי שמעון דאמר כל שאינו על מזבח החיצון אין בו משום פיגול, איכא למיפרך: מה להנך שכן פיגול פוסל בהן, תאמר בחטאות הפנימיות? ויש לומר דבפר העלם דבר של צבור כתיב "חטאת הקהל היא", ודריש מינה בת"כ שפסול שלא לשמו. אם כן אשכחן צבור וגם פנימי לעכב, ולמצוה ילפינן משלמים:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:2:1.english: (The correct reading is:) "All these are derived through mah hatzad" - Rabbeinu Tam asked: What [is true] of these, that they do not come as a poor man's offering? Would you say [the same] of these [other sin offerings]? And he answered: Since the poor man's offering itself is invalid if offered not for its own sake — that is, the sin offering of flour, which is invalid if offered not for its own sake, as we learned at the beginning of Menachot (2a), and we derive this from the verse "for it is a sin offering" — it is not logical that the fact that they come as a poor man's offering should cause them, in the wealthy form, to be valid when offered not for their own sake, since the poor man's offerings themselves are invalid. But there is a difficulty: if so, above, where [the Gemara] challenged regarding the leper, "What [is true] of these, that they do not come in poverty? Would you say [the same] of the leper?" — what is the challenge? Surely the poor man's offering is the bird sin offering, and the bird sin offering is invalid if offered not for its own sake, as we learned in the chapter Kodshei Kodashim (below, Zevachim 64b), and it is derived in Torat Kohanim from "it is a sin offering." And since it is invalid in the poor man's form, how can it cause the wealthy form to be valid when offered not for its own sake? And if you say: But regarding the sin offering of forbidden fat, [the Gemara] learned it from peace offerings by analogy (hekesh) for the mitzvah [aspect], so how do we derive the other sin offerings through mah hatzad? This is a question [raised] below in the chapter Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 50a): whether a matter learned through hekesh can then teach through a binyan av. [The answer is that] this is not a refutation at all, for all the sin offerings are also derived for the mitzvah [aspect] from peace offerings, and it is only for the [aspect of] being indispensable that we derive [the law] for the other sin offerings from these [three], since indispensability is written explicitly regarding them. And if you say: And the communal sin offerings, such as the goats of the new moons and festivals — from where do we know [their law]? They do not come through mah hatzad, for [one can say:] What [is true] of these, that a change of owner invalidates them, which is not so with a communal offering, as [the Gemara] said above (Zevachim 4a) that a change of owner does not apply to a communal [offering] as it does to an individual one. Even though a change of owner is not relevant to a communal [offering], it is nevertheless a good refutation, as we find in the first chapter of Kiddushin (5b): "What [is true] of money, that one can redeem consecrated items and second tithe with it? Would you say [the same] of betrothal by chuppah?" And so too in the chapter Hachovel (Bava Kamma 88a): "What [is true] of a woman, who is not [subject] to circumcision?" Furthermore, there is a difficulty regarding the inner sin offerings, according to Rabbi Shimon, who said that anything that is not [offered] on the outer altar has no piggul [status]: one can refute — What [is true] of these, that piggul invalidates them? Would you say [the same] of the inner sin offerings? And one can answer that regarding the bull for a communal unwitting error in a matter [of law], it is written "it is the sin offering of the congregation," and from this [the Sages] derive in Torat Kohanim that it is invalid if offered not for its own sake. Thus we have found a communal [offering] and also an inner one [that are indispensable], and for the mitzvah [aspect] we derive [the law] from peace offerings:

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:3:1.hebrew: הגה"ה בשאר ימות השנה לשמו פסול - היינו קודם הפסח, דבעי עקירה; או כגון דנדחו בעלים לפסח שני. אבל אח"כ לא, דפסח בשאר ימות השנה שלמים, ושלמים לשם פסח קשחיט, כדאמר בפ' תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף סד.) ובפ' שני דחולין (דף ל.). ומיהו איכא למ"ד בסוף אלו דברים (פסחים דף עג:) דבעי עקירה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:3:1.english: Gloss: "During the rest of the days of the year, [if sacrificed] for its sake, it is unfit" - This refers to [the period] before Passover, as it requires uprooting [of its status as a Paschal offering]; or, for example, where the owners were pushed off to the Second Passover. But afterward, no, because a Paschal offering during the rest of the days of the year is a peace offering, and a peace offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering [is fit], as stated in the chapter Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 64a) and in the second chapter of Chullin (30a). However, there is an opinion at the end of [the chapter] Elu Devarim (Pesachim 73b) that it requires uprooting.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:3:2.hebrew: לשמו פסול - (כתוב) בקונטרס: דלא חזו למילתייהו. ורבינו ש"י הגיה כדאמר בפסחים (דף סא.): שחטו קודם חצות — פסול, שנאמר "בין הערבים"; וכמה פעמים שנה הכתוב בקביעות זמנו בארבעה עשר בין הערבים. וסוגיא דהש"ס נמי משמע לקמן בגמרא: הפסח ששחטו שחרית, דמבין הערבים נפיק. ואין לומר דנפיק מדדרשינן הכא "לזבח שלמים", שצריך שיעקרנו לזבח שלמים, דדילמא הני מילי למצוה, אבל לעכב לא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:3:2.english: "For its sake, it is unfit" - (It is written) in the Kuntres [Rashi's commentary]: that they were not fit for their purpose. But Rabbeinu Shmuel (the Ri) emended [the text], as is stated in Pesachim (61a): If one slaughtered it before midday, it is unfit, as it is stated, "between the evenings"; and the verse repeated several times the fixed time of the fourteenth: "between the evenings." And the conclusion of the Talmud also implies this, later in the Gemara: the Paschal offering that one slaughtered in the morning, [that it is excluded] from "between the evenings." And one cannot say that it is excluded from what we expound here, "as a peace offering," that one must reassign it to be a peace offering, for perhaps these matters are only as a mitzvah [ideal], but not to be indispensable.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:5:1.hebrew: ואם מן הצאן קרבנו - פי' בקונטרס: לאו קרא יתירא דריש, אלא ממשמעות דקרא משמע ליה הכי. וזהו תימה, דאי לא מייתי קרא יתירא, מנא ליה לאוקומי בפסח? ונראה דמייתורא דריש, דלא הוה צריך למכתב "לזבח השלמים" דאשלמים קאי. [ועי"ל] דבסמוך דריש "כשב" לרבות פסח לאליה, ופירש רבינו ש"י דמיותר, דמדכתיב בתר הכי בשלמים "ואם מן העז קרבנו", מכלל דעד השתא איירי בכשב. וה"נ י"ל: מדכתיב לעיל "אם מן הבקר קרבנו", מכלל דהכא בצאן מיירי, אם כן "הצאן" מיותר הוא למותר פסח. ברוך:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:5:1.english: "And if his offering is from the flock" - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: He does not derive [the law] from a superfluous verse, but rather it is from the implication of the verse that he understands it so. But this is puzzling: for if he does not cite a superfluous verse, from where does he have [grounds] to establish [the verse] as referring to the Paschal offering? It appears that he derives it from a superfluity, as it was not necessary to write "for a sacrifice of peace offerings," since [the verse] is already speaking of peace offerings. [And furthermore,] shortly afterward [the Gemara] derives "lamb" as including the Paschal offering with regard to the fat tail. And Rabbeinu Shmuel (the Ri) explained that [the word] is superfluous, because since it is written afterward, regarding peace offerings, "And if his offering is from the goats," it follows that until now [the verse] was speaking of a lamb. And here too one can say: since it is written earlier, "If his offering is from the cattle," it follows that here [the verse] is speaking of the flock; if so, "the flock" is superfluous, to include the Paschal offering. Baruch.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:8:1.hebrew: אי הוה כתב לזבח השלמים כדקאמרת - הוה ליה למימר: אי הוה כתב "לזבח" כדקאמרת, דשלמים לא צריך כלל:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:8:1.english: If it had been written “for the sacrifice of the peace offerings,” as you say - [The Gemara] should have said: If it had been written merely “for a sacrifice,” as you say, [the word] “peace offerings” would not be necessary at all:
